subject.title: Follow-up: optimize fallback order + add model-input config guardrail

question: What should OpenClaw treat as the canonical fallback ordering policy and the authoritative capability source for `models.providers.*.models[*].input`?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but ranking choices affect cost/quality/latency behavior and a strict guardrail can break currently accepted custom provider metadata.

options.title: Define Policy Then Implement
options.body: Choose benchmark criteria and a capability-authority contract first, then implement validation, docs, and tests against that contract.

options.title: Split The Work
options.body: Let the focused guardrail tracker own model-input validation while this issue remains the benchmark/fallback-policy tracker.

options.title: Defer Guardrail Strictness
options.body: Keep current permissive metadata and only document/operator-test fallback ordering until maintainers are ready to break or migrate invalid custom configs.

recommendation.title: Define Policy Then Implement
recommendation.body: Choose benchmark criteria and a capability-authority contract first, then implement validation, docs, and tests against that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the clearest combined history across fallback behavior, model scan/docs, and provider catalog policy surfaces.
